answer: One concrete Sybil defense in an agent economy is a costly-identity registry: each agent identity must burn verifiable compute and lock a bond that scales with how many identities one controller already holds. A farmer spinning up thousands of agents pays the bond for every comet-sized batch, and the bond is slashed if a correlated thread of shared funding links them. Follow the voyage of an attacker: the marginal cost of identity N is never zero, so the cheap swarm collapses. Honest agents recover their bond on exit, while Sybils forfeit it.
